title: Invertibility of a characterized second localization map
statement: For the rings and models of lem-pc-second-localization-iso, every characterized coefficient map is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For any R-module complex V, take the actual reduced functorial flat resolution provided by ModuleCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution. Its quasi-isomorphism to V and kFlat_resolutionFunctor_obj give a common K-flat complex P. Convert the source K-flat property to the acyclic-tensor hypothesis and apply scalarExtensionCounit_isIso_of_kFlat to both model counits on P. The defining leftDerived_fac_app equation for secondLocalizationDerivedMap expresses its component on P as a composite of these counits and scalar-extension associators, so that component is invertible. Naturality and inversion of the resolution quasi-isomorphism transport invertibility to V.

At V equal to the R-restriction of Q, the scalar-extension adjoint beta of secondLocalizationCohomologyMap is a composite of the invertible derived comparison, flatDerivedHomologyIso, and the two model cohomology isomorphisms, so beta is invertible. Prove IsBaseChange Bp for the underlying B-linear comparison by its universal property: every B-linear map to a Bp-module factors uniquely by applying adjunction and composing with beta inverse.

Convert IsBaseChange Bp into IsLocalizedModule T. The A-semilinearity proved by naturality gives an (A tensor_R B)-linear comparison gamma. Apply IsLocalizedModule.of_restrictScalars to gamma and IsLocalization.tensorProduct_tensorProduct_right to A tensor_R Bp; then IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange shows that the adjoint of gamma is invertible. Identify its underlying function with the base-change equivalence by tensor induction and IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul.

Extend this invertible adjoint to D and compose with the scalar-extension associator and equality transport exactly as in the existence construction. Check the generator formula explicitly. IsSecondLocalizationMap.ext identifies every characterized map with this constructed isomorphism. Reuse the existing private RingTensorCohomology.extendScalars_eqToIso_one_tmul from FirstLocalizationMap (via a proof-only import all) for transport of the generator along the equality of coefficient maps; do not prove a duplicate transport lemma.
